_help: Every tunable constant of engine/mlearn.py. Changing a value here changes behaviour without a code edit; learning or the owner may tune them. Sources: docs/research/round2/03-routing-ml.md, 08-online-learning.md, 07-evaluation.md section 4.4.

state._help: Bounds that keep stats/ml.json small however long the brain runs.

bandit._help: Hierarchical discounted Beta-Bernoulli Thompson sampling (round2/03 sections 2.1-2.3). K_G and K_F are the capped pseudo-counts pulling class toward family toward global; gamma is the discount per update of an arm cell; n_cap bounds the discounted count; model_change_n is the effective count kept when an arm's model id changes; drift_gamma is the one-off extra discount a drift alarm applies to its class. min_outcomes and min_arms gate acting; near_best is delta; propensity_draws is the Monte-Carlo size.

explore._help: Safe exploration, invariant I-10. Cheaper arms are eligible only with a verifying check, risk in safe_risks and tier <= max_tier. At most max_rate of eligible tasks in the window explore, and wasted spend (failed explorations) stays under max_waste of window spend. exploit_margin and exploit_n decide when a cheaper arm counts as exploitation rather than exploration (10th-percentile pass rate within the margin of the baseline mean, with enough family evidence). The margin is 0.10, the owner tolerance of round2/03 section 2.6, not the 0.05 of section 2.4: with n_cap 40 the 10th percentile sits about 0.06 below the mean, so 0.05 made exploitation a coin flip even for an equally good arm (measured in tests/test_mlearn.py).

calibration._help: Estimate calibration (round2/08 section 4): log ratio actual/estimate, EW mean with half-life in tasks, pooled toward the family with K pseudo-tasks; quantiles from the last state.ratio_cap ratios; acts at min_n. Before that, p50 is the estimate and p80 is prior_p80_factor times it. drift_cap is the n a class keeps after a drift alarm.

drift._help: Drift charts per task class (round2/08 section 5, round2/07 section 4.4). Reference = first ref_n observations: median, and the larger of 1.4826 x MAD and the standard deviation (floored at sigma_floor); failure rate as a Beta upper estimate (mean + p0_z sd). EWMA on normalised log tokens (lam, L); Page-Hinkley on the same stream (delta and lambda in sigma units; lambda 8 as in round2/07); one-sided CUSUM on first-pass failures (k above the reference rate, threshold h). An alarm needs confirm_charts different charts within confirm_window observations, or the CUSUM signalling cusum_confirm times in a row (it is the only chart on its stream). Thresholds were set by simulation in tests/test_mlearn.py: about 7% of 200-task stationary runs raise any alarm. After an alarm the reference is rebuilt from the next ref_n observations; the alarm shows on boot until then.

credit._help: Memory credit (round2/08 section 3). Only followed items get credit; advantage = y - class baseline, split equally among followed items. Baseline is an EW mean of y with rate baseline_alpha from baseline_prior. Ranking multiplier = clamp(base + slope x lower bound, low, high) where the lower bound is mean - z x sd of the Beta posterior; neutral (1.0) until min_n followed uses. Owner-stated items always get high (I-08). correction_weight is the harmful mass an owner correction naming an item adds.

flaky._help: Gate flakiness: Beta(prior_a + pass-after-fail on an unchanged commit, prior_b + failures that stayed failed). A score >= rerun means re-run once before calling it red; >= investigate is flagged in the report.

retention._help: Usage-based forgetting (round2/08 section 11): R = exp(-t/S), t = days since last followed use; S starts at s0_days by item type and grows by growth per followed use, capped at cap_days; importance 3 multiplies S by important_factor. Owner-stated and standing items do not decay. learn decay proposes demotion when R < threshold.

review._help: Review stopping by capture-recapture (Chapman). Another round only if the estimated remaining blocking defects >= min_remaining; the estimate is used only when the overlap is >= min_overlap, otherwise overlap that small means many are likely unseen and another round is run; never more than max_rounds.

sizing._help: Learned sizing in shadow (round2/08 section 6): multinomial Naive Bayes over salted word hashes, Laplace alpha, likelihood damped by 1/sqrt(words), rule tier as prior (rule_prior, the rest shared). A hint needs min_strong strong labels, posterior >= min_conf and a one-step difference; weak labels count weak_weight. act stays false until shadow evidence earns it; even then it only lowers a tier (I-11).

offline._help: Offline policy check by self-normalised inverse propensity scoring (round2/03 section 2.6): weights clipped at clip; trusted only with effective sample size >= min_ess and >= min_per_arm logged runs per arm.

report._help: Owner report wording thresholds (round2/03 section 2.7): fewer than too_early effective outcomes = too early; below medium = LOW; below high = MEDIUM; else HIGH.
